body:
[R86] POSITIVE - exact head e2f7c0c0ada3cce2a3ef7a9e895db6e58f54321f Round R86-9 of PR #428 (issue #413). Tree 5e4d4e29c4cf6f193ea89ac8f702c67d288b80bc, base 55518b470935f5478e0879bfc4ff183cc5d5ccc4, ten commits on the base. Reviewed in an isolated public clone detached at that head with the three public submodules at their pinned commits; nothing outside `REVIEW.md` and `review-evidence/` was written, every temporary mutation was applied to the tracked file and restored with its sha256 compared before and after. Verdict: POSITIVE. All three acceptance criteria of #413 are met and I reproduced each of them. Three MINOR findings are open, all of them about the TERMINATION CLAIM rather than about the type-7 reading the issue asks for, and all three concern shapes that no tracked file carries. `RTL` is banked clean. `Conformance`, `Robustness`, `Tests` and `Docs` are not. ## What this round measured Independent instruments, all in `review-evidence/`: 1. A renderer oracle of my own (`oracle.py`), 106 synthetic rows through GitHub's Markdown rendering API in gfm mode, comparing the headings `gen_toc.headings()` lists with the headings the renderer emits. The same rows were then replayed against the walk at the base, at the round-7 head, at the round-8 head and here (`rows_at.py`, `rows-at-heads.txt`). 2. A structural probe of `_class_guards()` on synthetic module sources (`probe_guard.py`), which touches no file at all. 3. Bounded reversion controls on the tracked `scripts/gen_toc.py` (`controls.py`, `controls2.py`), sha256 verified before and after each one. 4. An end-to-end run of the shipped em-dash gate over scratch repositories (`e2e_exemption.py`), which is the only instrument that answers whether the exemption is actually granted. 5. A per-page dump of `blocks()`, `headings()` and `generated_block()` over all 159 tracked pages at the base and at this head (`perpage.py`). Renderer agreement over my 106 rows, walk against renderer: | head | AGREE | ESCAPE (walk keeps a heading the renderer hides) | WITHHOLD | |---|---:|---:|---:| | base 55518b47 | 37 | 64 | 5 | | round 7, 2e86442d | 69 | 30 | 7 | | round 8, e0315b19 | 72 | 27 | 7 | | this head, e2f7c0c0 | 84 | 19 | 3 | The change closes 45 of the 64 escapes my rows found at the base and introduces none. The 19 that remain are four families, and every one of them answers identically at the base, at round 7, at round 8 and here: 13 rows in the type-1 closing-tag site (F1 below), 2 in the fence closer at a refused character (F2 below), 1 in the container content column of #437, and 3 in HTML block types 3 to 5. The last two families are declared truthfully in `blocks()` and in the PR limitations, with the right direction, and my rows confirm both. ## Does the termination claim hold? Partly, and not as stated. The round asked me to try to break it four ways. **A decision site the enumeration does not see: YES, several.** `_class_guards()` collects sites from two places only: module-level `ast.Assign` nodes with `ast.Name` targets that contain a `.compile(` call (`scripts/gen_toc.py:854`), and `ast.Call` nodes with an `ast.Attribute` func inside the functions reachable from `WALK_ROOTS` (`scripts/gen_toc.py:858`). Measured on synthetic sources (`probe_guard.out`) and then on the tracked file (`controls.out`): - an annotated binding, `X: re.Pattern = re.compile(...)`, is not an `ast.Assign`, so the site vanishes. Control C3 rebinds `BLOCK_QUOTE_RE` that way on the tracked file: `--sites` drops from 26 to 25, no `GUARD` note is printed, and `--selftest` still reports `PASS (267/267 arm(s))`. No arm pins the site count: `_class_guard_arms()` asserts that the note list is empty and that both kinds are present, never how many sites there are. - a tuple-target assignment and `from re import compile` lose the site the same way (probes A2 and A3). - a decision reached through a module-level alias or a module-level lambda is outside the call walk (probes A11 and A13). **A spelling the guard does not refuse: YES.** The guard refuses a hand-spelled class in a compiled expression and in a `strip`, and nothing else. Measured: - a membership test. Control C1 replaces `char not in CLASSES["blank"]` with `char not in " \t"` at `scripts/gen_toc.py:277`, the walk's own indentation decision: 26 sites, no `GUARD` note, `PASS (267/267)`. Control C2 widens the same inline class with a character of its own: same result. That decision is the one that says whether a line is an indented code block, which is what gates the type-7 escape under a heading, and it is neither enumerated nor judged. - `str.startswith`, `endswith`, `replace`, `find`, `count`, `partition`, `index`, `removeprefix`, `translate` and `split` WITH an argument all carry a class past the guard (probes A6 and A7, control C5). A bare `split()` is a refusal site, so the asymmetry is deliberate for `strip` and accidental everywhere else. - inside an expression the guard does judge, a blank flanked by two alphanumerics is exempted by the heuristic at `scripts/gen_toc.py:846`, so `[a b]` passes (probes A8 and A9). That exemption exists for `GENERATED_RE`'s prose and is reasonable; it is simply not airtight. The `_class_guards()` docstring declares what it cannot see as "a class reached through `getattr`, built at run time or imported ... as does a rule the walk never calls" (`scripts/gen_toc.py:816`). None of the shapes above is any of those. They are ordinary Python, written plainly, at module level or in the walk. **A class the table does not own: YES, one that matters.** See F1. The class between a type-1 name and its closing angle bracket is spelled `\s` and classified REFUSAL, and the renderer's class at that position is empty. **A position where a single-sourced class is the wrong class: none found.** Every one of the 16 bodies in `CLASSES` matched the renderer at the position that reads it over my rows: the 53-row tag-grammar sweep agrees on 52 (`oracle-rows-tag.txt`), and the twelve class rows B1 to B12 all agree (`oracle-rows-head.txt`). The three inline single characters the walk still spells outside the table are the tab in `_indent_columns`, the backtick in `_opens` and the pipe in `line_kinds` and `_table_cells`; each is the right character for its position, and the pipe is the only one the table also owns (`CLASSES["cell stop"]`), which is a cosmetic inconsistency rather than a defect. **Is the refusal at the three #440 sites honest?** For one of the three, yes. For the other two, no: it refuses nothing that matters. `REFUSED` is exactly right as a set, verified independently over the whole code space: `str.isspace()`, `str.strip()` and the expression engine's `\s` name the identical set of characters, and `REFUSED` is that set less the space, the tab and the line feed, 26 characters, and no tracked file carries one of them (`probe_refused.out`, and 0 of 768 tracked readable text files). The argument the head builds on it is sound for the fence closer, where the renderer's own class really is the blank: rows E1 and E2 need a no-break space or a form feed to diverge, and row E3 with ordinary spaces agrees. It is not sound for the two type-1 closers, and that is F1. ## Findings ```text [R86] MINOR Conformance, Robustness, Docs - scripts/gen_toc.py:462 and :489 (the type-1 closer), declared at :99 and :811 - the two type-1 closing-tag sites are declared held by the refusal, and the refusal cannot see what escapes them Requirement/evidence: `_still_open()` and `_opens()` read a type-1 block's end with `re.search(r"" % tag, line, re.IGNORECASE)`. `_class_guards()` classifies both as REFUSAL, on the stated ground that "it spells Python's own whitespace, whose excess over the renderer's blank is exactly `REFUSED`, so a page that could tell the two apart is refused before the site is asked" (scripts/gen_toc.py:810). That premise does not hold at this position: the renderer admits NO character between a type-1 name and its closing angle bracket, so the excess over the renderer's class there is `REFUSED` plus the space and the tab, and neither of those is refused. Measured against GitHub's renderer, 13 rows escape at this head with ordinary characters (review-evidence/oracle-rows-refusal.txt, rows F1 to F9 and G1, and oracle-rows-head.txt rows A1, A2, A4, A6): `
` ... `
` has the walk close the block and list the heading after it, where the renderer keeps the block open and shows no heading at all. ``, ``, ``, ``, `` and `` behave the same, and so does the closer inside a longer line. The same site runs the other way too: the renderer ends a type-1 block at any of the four closing tags, the walk only at the one that opened it, so `
` closed by `` withholds a heading
  the page shows (oracle-rows-head.txt row A5). End to end through the shipped
  gate, case T2 of review-evidence/e2e-exemption.out grants the exemption for a
  Contents label copied from a heading the base page does not render, with no
  refused character anywhere on either version of the page.
Impact: the exemption #413 exists to withhold is granted one position over, for
  a label that mirrors a heading the base page renders as raw HTML, so the entry
  keeps a U+2014 and points at an anchor the page does not have. Reachability
  today is nil: no tracked file carries a type-1 closing tag at all, and the
  reading itself is byte-identical at the base, at round 7 and at round 8, so
  this change neither introduces nor widens it. What is new at this head is the
  claim that the refusal holds it, which is what makes the family look closed.
Required change: either read the renderer's end condition at these two sites
  (a literal `
`, ``, `` or ``, any of the four ending any type-1 block), which is #440's work, or correct the three places that say the refusal holds them (scripts/gen_toc.py:99, :810, and the PR's "Known limitations" bullet on #440) to say what is measured: the refusal holds the fence closer, and the two type-1 closers are an open escape reachable with a space or a tab. A REFUSAL site should not be accepted without naming the renderer's class at that position, since the whole argument is a claim about the difference between the two. Verification: rerun review-evidence/rows_r86_9b.py; rows F1 to F9 and G1 must AGREE, or the limitation must name them. Case T2 of e2e_exemption.py must report a finding rather than an exempt label. ``` ```text [R86] MINOR Conformance, Tests, Docs - scripts/check_em_dash.py:210-217 (`base_labels`), against scripts/gen_toc.py:283-303 (`refusals`) - the refusal is wired into the head side of the exemption only, and the base side is what decides it Requirement/evidence: `refusals()` and its wiring are this head's central new safety mechanism, and the head states its reach as "a page carrying one of those is not walked at all ... it obtains no provenance, and no label copied from it can be exempt". The gate applies it twice, both times to the HEAD text of the page: `judge_page` calls `refusal_notes(change.path, text)` on `git show HEAD:path`, and `generated_block` refuses the same text. But the AUTHORITY for the exemption is the BASE version: `base_labels()` runs `headings(git show base:path)` with no refusal check at all. A page that carries a refused character at the base and not at the head therefore obtains its exemption from a walk that was never refused. Measured end to end: case T3 of review-evidence/e2e-exemption.out, a base page whose fence closer is padded with one no-break space, where the renderer keeps the fence open and shows no heading (review-evidence/oracle-rows-refusal.txt row E1) and the gate grants the exemption with 0 findings. Impact: the one shape the refusal was added to stop, at the one site it was added for, passes when it sits on the base version of the page. No tracked page carries any of the 26 characters, so nothing on the tree is affected. Required change: refuse the base text where the exemption is decided, so that a base page the walk does not read authorises no label, with an arm that fails when the call is removed. The existing round-9 control plants its character in the HEAD page only, so it does not reach this path. Verification: case T3 of review-evidence/e2e_exemption.py must report a finding and exempt nothing; a new control in `_provenance_controls()` planting the character in the BASE page must fail when the refusal on `base_labels` is reverted. ``` ```text [R86] MINOR Tests, Docs - scripts/gen_toc.py:798-880 (`_class_guards`) and scripts/gen_toc_cases.py:762-848 (`_class_guard_arms`) - the enumeration can lose a site silently, and the guard passes ordinary spellings its docstring implies it refuses Requirement/evidence: the claim that closes the family by construction is that "a decision added later is in the enumeration whether or not anyone remembers it" (scripts/gen_toc.py:806). Measured on the tracked file with sha256 verified before and after each control (review-evidence/controls.out): C3 rebinds one compiled expression as an annotated assignment, `--sites` falls from 26 to 25, no GUARD note is printed and `--selftest` still passes 267/267, because no arm pins the site count. C1 spells the walk's own indentation class inline at its own decision site, and C2 widens it there: both silent, both 267/267. C5 puts a class of its own in a `startswith()` in the walk: silent. On synthetic sources (review-evidence/probe_guard.out) a tuple-target binding, `from re import compile`, a module-level alias, a module-level lambda, eight further `str` methods, `split` with an argument, and a blank flanked by alphanumerics inside a judged expression all pass. The docstring's declared blind spots are "a class reached through `getattr`, built at run time or imported ... as does a rule the walk never calls"; none of the shapes above is one of those. The control C6, the same widening written inside a compiled expression, is caught with a GUARD note and two failing arms, which is the subset the guard really covers. Impact: the guard is a useful structural proxy over compiled expressions and strips, and it is presented as a closure over every decision site. A later contributor who writes a membership test, a `startswith`, or an annotated binding gets no signal, and the site is not in `--sites` either, so the enumeration a reader consults to check the claim does not list it. Required change: state the real reach in the docstring (compiled module-level `ast.Assign` expressions, `re.*` calls and strips inside the walk, and nothing else), and add the two cheap arms that make a silent loss loud: one pinning the number of sites `--sites` prints, and one refusing a class spelled in a membership test or a `str` method inside the walk. Verification: control C3 of review-evidence/controls.py must fail an arm rather than print 25 sites at 267/267; control C1 must print a GUARD note. ``` ## Clean lens ```text [R86] PASS RTL - `git diff --name-only 55518b47..e2f7c0c0` (three files, all under scripts/), plus check_rtl_source_lists.py, check_sweep_shape.py and check_hygiene.py --check at this head - no HDL, pin, constraint, workflow or suite inventory changed ``` The diff at this head touches `scripts/gen_toc.py`, `scripts/gen_toc_cases.py` and `scripts/check_em_dash.py` and nothing else: `hdl/`, `tb/`, `syn/`, `constraints/`, `sw/`, `tools/`, `configs/`, `.github/` and `docs/` are all absent from it, which I checked by path filter rather than by reading the summary. The inventories that would notice a change nonetheless all pass: `check_rtl_source_lists.py` reports the 100-file `milan_datapath` closure carried by 4 of 4 consumer lists and 32 of 38 protocol-processor tops with the 6 recorded omissions, `check_sweep_shape.py` passes, and the hygiene ratchet passes over 3 populations and 653 files with CRLF at 0. No clock, reset, CDC, width or backpressure question is reachable from a documentation generator, and naming that is what covers the lens here. ## The questions this round was asked **Conformance. A heading wrapped in a type-7 block yields no exemption (acceptance 1).** Met, and reproduced three ways. The shipped gate's own type-7 control holds (`check_em_dash.py --selftest`, 33 arms, including the `` wrapped heading, the `
` twin, the legitimate mirrored label and the fence-in-comment page). Reverting the classification drives it red: control R3 in `controls2.out` removes the type-7 branch and the gate exits 2 naming its control three ways, while the TOC self-test falls to 156 of 267; control R1 restores a blank-line guard on the tag and 46 arms fail; control N18 hands out provenance for a refused page and the gate exits 2 again. Against the renderer, the whole type-7 family agrees: 52 of my 53 tag-grammar rows and all eleven predecessor rows C1 to C10 (`oracle-rows-tag.txt`, `oracle-rows-head.txt`). **Is "cannot interrupt a paragraph" read as "opens only after a blank line"?** No longer, and that is the right answer. The head reads it as "opens only while no paragraph is open", tracked by `_paragraph_after()` with a HELD state, which is the faithful reading of CommonMark 4.6: the blank line is sufficient but not necessary, and any block that closed leaves no paragraph open. I measured the difference rather than reading it: at the base, rows C2 to C10 all escaped; at this head all ten agree with the renderer. **Can it ever hide a heading that renders?** Yes, in three measured shapes, all of them pre-existing and all of them declared. A setext heading is never listed (row C9; `HEAD_RE` is ATX-only, #437, declared). A line mixing visible text and a comment opener labels the rest of the page as commented (the `
